task_text: In units c=1, event B minus event A in frame S has delta_t=3 and delta_x=5. Frame S' moves at v=+0.8 along x relative to S. Use t'=gamma(t-vx), x'=gamma(x-vt). A separate particle has velocity u=+0.6 in S. Return answer keys gamma, delta_t_prime, delta_x_prime, interval_t2_minus_x2, particle_velocity_prime, separation_type (timelike/spacelike/null), reversed_order (boolean), simultaneous_frame_velocity. Give numeric values, not expressions. Distinguish the event-pair displacement from the separate particle velocity.

response.concise_method_summary: gamma = 1/sqrt(1-v^2) = 1/sqrt(1-0.64) = 1.666667. Applied t'=gamma(t-vx), x'=gamma(x-vt) with t=3, x=5, v=0.8: t' = 1.666667*(3-4) = -1.666667; x' = 1.666667*(5-2.4) = 4.333333. Invariant interval t^2-x^2 = 9-25 = -16, confirmed equal in primed frame (t'^2-x'^2 = 2.7778-18.7778 = -16). Since |Δx|>|Δt| the separation is spacelike, so no frame-independent time order exists; here Δt=3>0 but Δt'=-1.6667<0, so the temporal order is reversed in S' specifically — this reversal is only physically permitted because the pair is spacelike (timelike/null pairs preserve order in all frames). The frame in which the two events are simultaneous has velocity v_sim = Δt/Δx = 3/5 = 0.6 (from setting t'=0 in the transform); this exists because 0.6<1. Separately, the particle's velocity in S' uses relativistic velocity addition: u' = (u-v)/(1-uv) = (0.6-0.8)/(1-0.48) = -0.2/0.52 = -0.384615. Note: v_sim = 0.6 numerically coincides with the particle's u = 0.6 in S, but these are unrelated quantities — one is derived purely from the event-pair displacement (Δt/Δx), the other is the separate particle's velocity transformed via the addition law; the match is coincidental to the chosen numbers.
assumptions: Units with c=1 throughout, so v and u are dimensionless fractions of c
v=+0.8 is the velocity of S' relative to S along the shared x-axis, standard Lorentz boost convention
The 'separate particle' velocity u=0.6 is a value in frame S, unrelated to the event pair (Δt=3, Δx=5)
simultaneous_frame_velocity refers to the frame in which the two given events (A and B) are simultaneous, found from Δt'=0
reversed_order refers to the temporal order of events A and B as seen in S' compared to S
proposed_verification: Recompute t'^2 - x'^2 and confirm it equals t^2 - x^2 = -16 (Lorentz invariance check)
Verify |v_sim|<1 so the simultaneous frame is physically realizable (0.6<1, passes)
Confirm separation_type via sign of interval: negative (t^2-x^2<0) implies spacelike, matching |Δx|>|Δt|
Check particle_velocity_prime via addition law is in (-1,1): -0.384615 passes
Independently verify reversed_order by checking sign of Δt' differs from sign of Δt only possible for spacelike separations
